complete_examples.text: To simulate the train-track system in time domain, an implicit direct integration method, i.e., Houbolt method [20] , is applied to solve the dynamic equations of motion.
Houbolt method is a multistep (three-step) method by utilizing the information on the system at previous three time steps to predict displacement, velocity and acceleration of the current station.
Houbolt method, an unconditionally stable implicit numerical integral method, is applied to solve the dynamic equations of motion for vehicle–track systems.
In this paper, the Houbolt method and Cholesky decomposition are combined to solve the dynamic equation.
For the linear elastic dynamic system, the response of system can be directly through the step-by-step time-domain numerical method, i.e., Houbolt method [56].
For the vehicle-rail subsystem, the response of subsystem can be solved by the stepwise time-domain integral method, with the Houbolt method applied in this work.
